communityCloud.source: Installer authorization built from externally injected publicKeys and revokedKeyIds, plus the matching durable install journal/current receipt for installationId and accepted runtime sequence. S11 already forbids deriving approved owner or installation identity from observed or fetched values.
communityCloud.delivery: For the current per-installation release, the installer supplies a closed nonsecret trust object to build-release before Vite runs: publicKeys, revokedKeyIds, minSequence and expectedInstallationId. build-release verifies the manifest against that object, then embeds the same immutable object in the built client. It must not construct expectedInstallationId or minSequence from the manifest it is verifying.
communityCloud.initialInstall: Use the verified authorization and newly committed journal/receipt only after owner evidence passes. Missing trust object is a pre-fetch trust_missing failure.
communityCloud.update: Use the previous installed journal/receipt as the floor and the external revoked-key list; advance the floor only after the new signed update is accepted and promoted.
communityCloud.rollback: Artifact version may roll back only through the approved release path; the rollback operation still issues a higher trusted sequence. Browser floor never moves backward.

localSingle.source: DPAPI CurrentUser protected install record owned by E7, combined with packaged release trust and revocation state. The record supplies expectedInstallationId, last accepted sequence and endpoint binding independently of the fetched manifest.
localSingle.delivery: Electron main reads the protected record and passes only the nonsecret trust tuple to the renderer in memory through the future isolated preload. No localStorage, IndexedDB, cookie, URL or cache storage.
localSingle.lifecycle: Create atomically at install, advance only after verified update, preserve monotonic sequence on rollback, and fail closed on unreadable or mismatched DPAPI state.

localOffice.source: Office installer or local service protected install record plus packaged release trust. The institution CA/TLS connection authenticates the service, but the fetched manifest still does not become its own expected state.
localOffice.delivery: Serve or preload the nonsecret expectedInstallationId, sequence floor and revocation trust from the protected local installation context before manifest acceptance. Browser persistence remains forbidden.
localOffice.lifecycle: Server install creates the record; signed update advances it; rollback keeps a higher operation sequence; missing or unreadable state blocks startup. E8 owns the exact runtime mechanism.
